Recovery to $8.62 by 2026-07-06 with no company catalyst; $7.90 now.
ruling: DE-RATE on a cyclical whose DERAILMENT already completed (FY22-FY24) and STOPPED. Adjusted EBITDA margin has been 10.5% in FY24, 10.5% in FY25, and is guided 10.5-11.0% for FY26 - an impaired brand does not hold a flat margin for three years while opening showrooms. FY25 growth was honestly composed (delivered comp +3.6% PLUS ~+4.9% non-comp), so unit growth is NOT masking negative comps. The brand is not impaired; the cycle is real and largely priced at 6.1x EV/EBITDA. But the FY26 guide is back-end loaded (FY comp delivered 0-3% with Q1 at -1.7% and Q2 guided -5% to 0% requires H2 of roughly +2% to +6%) and gets its first honest test in three days.

freezable_call.basis: Q2'26 laps an easy -3.6% and management stated demand improved as Q1 progressed - both favour the inflection. Against that, the series is genuinely volatile (+4.1 / -3.6 / +7.4 / -2.8 / -5.7) and big-ticket discretionary demand has no momentum property to lean on. Barely better than a coin flip - which is itself the finding: the FY26 guide rests on a coin flip resolving in three days while the stock sits 41.8% off its low.

edge_explainer: The bear on Arhaus is 'discretionary big-ticket plus frozen housing', and the honest answer is that it is CYCLICAL, not an impaired brand - and I can date exactly when the damage stopped. GAAP operating margin fell 15.0% -> 12.8% -> 6.8% across FY22-FY24, and then Adjusted EBITDA margin sat at 10.5% in FY24, 10.5% in FY25, and is guided 10.5-11.0% for FY26. Three flat years is a normalisation signature, not an impairment one. The decomposition also clears management: FY25 revenue +8.5% was delivered-comp +3.6% PLUS ~+4.9% of new/relocated boxes - both legs positive, so showroom growth is NOT masking negative comps. The balance sheet is genuinely, not optically, strong: no funded debt, $177M cash (16% of market cap), and a lease-adjusted EV/EBITDAR of 6.6x that agrees with the 6.1x unadjusted EV/EBITDA, so there is no hidden lease leverage. The strongest single finding is anti-masking: into a weak tape this management ADDED disclosure rather than reducing it - voluntarily publishing quarterly Comparable Written (the leading, worse) and Delivered Sales schedules plus showroom-portfolio and square-footage detail, putting the -5.7% written comp in the Q1 highlight bullets, pre-warning that Q2 laps a distorted quarter, and explicitly excluding a potential IEEPA tariff refund from guidance. Under house doctrine the absence of expected masking is itself a positive microstructure finding, and it is why the reaffirmed guide reads as a real forecast rather than a stall. So why only 4/10: the edge is +7.8%, well inside my own scenario error bars; the FY26 guide is back-end loaded and its first test is in three days; and the path check fails outright - +41.8% off a 75-day-old low is the last leg of a bounce, not a dislocation. This is a fairly-paid risk with bounded tails, ownable at a price that pays for the cyclical variance. $7.90 is not that price; $7.00 and below is.
honesty_grade: CLEAN - ANTI-MASKING POSITIVE. No takeaway-vs-data divergence found. In 2026 the company voluntarily added quarterly Comparable Written / Comparable Delivered Sales schedules, showroom-portfolio composition, gross square footage, showroom-maturity and per-state detail; disclosed the -5.7% written comp in the Q1 highlight bullets rather than a table; pre-warned that Q2'26 laps a distorted prior-year quarter (in-housed Dallas DC ramped ahead of schedule); and explicitly excluded a potential IEEPA tariff refund from guidance while stating in the 10-Q that no receivable has been or will be recognised until realisable. Increasing granularity into a weak tape is the opposite of the masking reflex - catalog it.
